newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Discount Bank Q4 net down.
newsitem.headline: Israel Discount Bank Q4 net down.

text.p: (in millions of shekels except earnings per share)

Income was influenced by a significant increase in the provision for doubtful debts in the fourth quarter, caused by, among other factors, a stricter valuation of a number of borrowers in the construction sector and a decline in the profitability of a banking subsidiary.
Yield on shareholders' equity was 6.0 percent compared with 7.3 percent in 1995.
Total consolidated assets at year-end reached 80.1 billion shekels against 77.3 billion at the end of 1995.
Total credit to the public amounted to 44.0 billion shekels against 40.9 billion at the end of 1995 while deposits rose to 66.9 billion shekels from 64.7 billion.

"The rise in total assets, credit and deposits was moderate, despite an increase in operations because of an erosion of the value of assets and liabilities denominated in foreign currency. This resulted from the lag in the rise of the foreign currency rate, compared to the rise in the CPI (consumer price index), reducing assets by approximately three percent," the bank said in a statement.
Shareholders' equity rose to 4.2 billion shekels from 4.0 billion at the end of 1995.
The ratio of shareholders' equity to total risk assets was 8.5 percent against 8.7 percent the previous year.

To improve the capital ratio the bank is raising secondary capital. In December and January the bank issued non-negotiable deferred notes to institutional investors and intends to issue to the public additional deferred noted through a prospectus to be published shortly.
